articles.summary: it's the first day of practice at the Presidents Cup, the golf tournament happening at the famed Medinah County Club Golf Course.
articles.body:
It's the first day of practice at the Presidents Cup, the golf tournament happening at the famed Medinah County Club Golf Course.

It's been years in the making, and now is just days away from the start of The President's Cup here at Medinah Country Club. And what a week it's going be.

Medinah is rolling out the red carpet for some the best golfers in the world. The President's Cup is a bi-annual event pitting the U.S. Team against a team made up of the best international players outside of Europe.

Medinah is no stranger to major golf events.

President Trump is visiting Chicago sometime in the coming days for the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club.

Mike Gilligan with the Chicago District for Golf Association talks about the Presidents Cup.

Mike Gilligan from the Chicago District Golf Association said hosting the President's Cup puts Medinah in a very special place in golf history.

"This place just never disappoints," Gilligan said. "It is one of the greatest arenas to host a major exhibition, championship or otherwise. I think its location means everything. It is so easy to get to form the North Shore, from the south suburbs and the western suburbs. I just think it is the ultimate venue in golf here in Chicago."

It takes more than a village to pull off a massive event like this. Volunteers come from around the area to serve as marshals around the course and work the merchandise tent.

"We have two types of marshals," Paul Grane said. "We have roving marshals and we have hole marshals. The roving marshal committee is a group of 46 people that volunteered to basically act as fore caddies during the tournament. There are four people per match. As balls go left or right, our team are the people that actually go to the balls, help with spectator management, help them get out of the way so the match can carry on and then we stay ahead of the match every time.

Besides being a great event for fans, The President's Cup generates millions of dollars for charity. Several local organizations like the Chicago District Golf Association and the First Tee have already received generous donations.

The Tournament starts on Thursday morning and ends on Sunday.

articles.title: Falcons vs. Packers bold predictions for Thursday Night Football clash in Week 3
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons (0-2) head to Lambeau Field to face the Green Bay Packers (1-1) in a Week 3 Thursday Night Football showdown that carries far more weight...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons (0-2) head to Lambeau Field to face the Green Bay Packers (1-1) in a Week 3 Thursday Night Football showdown that carries far more weight than a typical September game. Green Bay enters as roughly a 7-point home favorite with the total set around 44.5, and Atlanta arrives desperate to avoid an 0-3 hole with Michael Penix Jr. cleared to start after being listed with a knee injury. It's the Packers' long-awaited home opener, and both rosters are dealing with notable absences, from Jawaan Taylor and A.J. Terrell nursing injuries for Atlanta to Green Bay's own banged-up unit. Here are three bold predictions for this early-season measuring stick.

Michael Penix Jr. Silences the Doubters With a Multi-Touchdown Night

Michael Penix's return under center is the single biggest storyline heading into Thursday, and the bold call here is that he doesn't just play, he thrives. After being ruled out and then cleared through the week, Penix gets a green light against a Packers defense that has shown vulnerabilities against mobile, quick-releasing quarterbacks early in the season.

Expect Atlanta's coaching staff to lean on quick-hitting concepts and play-action to protect their banged-up offensive line, particularly with Taylor questionable at right tackle. Penix throws for at least two touchdowns and pushes 250-plus passing yards, connecting early and often with Drake London to keep the Falcons competitive against the spread even if Green Bay controls the scoreboard late. The bigger surprise wouldn't be Penix struggling in his return, it would be him outplaying Jordan Love 's overall efficiency for large stretches of the game.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Green Bay's Ground Game Disappoints, Forcing Love Into a 35-Pass Attempt Night

Green Bay's home opener hype will center on a run-heavy identity, but the bold prediction is that the Packers can't establish anything consistent on the ground against Atlanta's front seven. That shifts the burden squarely onto Jordan Love , who ends up throwing the ball more than 35 times as Green Bay searches for answers.

With the Falcons' secondary already thin at cornerback due to Terrell's groin issue, Love finds success spreading the ball to his receiving corps, and one pass-catcher in particular becomes the story of the night by clearing 90 receiving yards. The offensive imbalance doesn't cost Green Bay the win, but it makes the game far closer through three quarters than the near touchdown spread would suggest, and it sets up a nervy finish at Lambeau.

Under 44.5 Cashes as Both Defenses Bend but Don't Break

Despite the offensive talent on both sides, the bold prediction for the scoreboard is that this game stays under the posted total of 44.5, with defense and turnovers defining the outcome more than explosive plays. Atlanta's defense, even without full strength up front, gets at least one takeaway off Love in the red zone that swings field position, while Green Bay's defense forces a similar mistake from Penix in his first real test back from injury.

Both teams settle for field goals on multiple scoring drives rather than converting touchdowns in the red zone, a common theme for divisional and cross-conference games this early in the season when timing and chemistry are still developing. Green Bay wins a game that finishes closer to 24-17 than a blowout, covering the spread comfortably while the under hits, rewarding bettors who trust that this Thursday night clash will be decided by execution in the trenches rather than a shootout through the air.

articles.title: How does the Presidents Cup work? Everything you need to know as the U.S. team takes on the International team at Medinah
articles.summary: The Presidents Cup is up for grabs this week in Chicago.
articles.body:
The golf world is headed to Medinah Country Club in Illinois this week to watch a dozen of the best American golfers go up against their non-European international counterparts in the classic match play competition. But unlike the Ryder Cup, this event has been completely dominated by the United States since its inception in the mid-1990s.

If the Americans can pull off the win come Sunday afternoon, it will mark their 11th straight victory. They've never lost on American soil, either.

Here's everything you need to know to keep up with the 2026 Presidents Cup.

The Presidents Cup is essentially just another version of the Ryder Cup, except this time, Europe isn't involved.

The United States fields a 12-man team to take on the International team, which is a 12-man group made up of non-European international players. The event is held every other year opposite of the Ryder Cup.

The Presidents Cup is taking place at Medinah Country Club in suburban Chicago. It marks the fifth different venue in the United States to host the tournament in the event's history. Medinah has hosted plenty of major golf events in the past, including three U.S. Opens, a pair of PGA Championships and the Ryder Cup back in 2012.

The Presidents Cup follows a simple format over four days, one extra day than the Ryder Cup.

Thursday will feature five four-ball matches, and then Friday will have five foursomes matches (more on these below). Saturday will include a doubleheader, with four-ball matches taking place in the morning and then foursomes matches taking place in the afternoon. Finally, all 12 players will square off in a singles match on Sunday.

There are 30 total points available, and the first team to reach 15.5 points wins the Presidents Cup. Players earn a full point for a match that they win, and each team earns half a point for matches that end in a tie.

Foursomes is better known as "alternate shot." Two teams of two square off against each other, with the two golfers on each team alternating each shot throughout the round.

Four-ball has each golfer play their ball through the hole, but then the team takes the lower score. That's frequently known as "best ball."

Brandt Snedeker is the captain for the U.S. team, and Geoff Ogilvy is the captain for the International team. Snedeker was an assistant captain at the 2024 Presidents Cup, and he's set to serve as a vice captain at the Ryder Cup next fall. Ogilvy has played on the International Team three times himself, and has been an assistant captain at the last four tournaments.

Just like the Ryder Cup, the top six golfers from each group earned a spot on the team through a qualifying system. Then the captains make six selections to fill out the team.

Scottie Scheffler Cameron Young Wyndham Clark Sam Burns Russell Henley Collin Morikawa Chris Gotterup Justin Thomas Xander Schauffele Patrick Cantlay Jackson Koivun Jacob Bridgeman

Si Woo Kim Hideki Matsuyama Ryan Fox Tom Kim Min Woo Lee Adam Scott Sungjae Im Nico Echavarria Corey Conners Nick Taylor Christiaan Bezuidenhout Ryo Hisatsune

The next two Presidents Cup sites have already been decided.

The 2028 Presidents Cup will be held at Kingston Heath Golf Club in Melbourne, Australia. It marks the fourth time the Presidents Cup is being held in Melbourne, and the first of two future stops. It will return there in 2040.

Then, in 2030, the Presidents Cup will return to the United States and be held at Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis. The iconic course most recently hosted the PGA Championship in 2018. The BMW Championship was held there this past season on the PGA Tour, too.

The United States rolled to an 18.5-11.5 win at the 2024 Presidents Cup at Royal Montreal. That actually marked the Americans' 10th straight Presidents Cup win.

The Americans won the inaugural event in a landslide in 1994, and hold a 13-1-1 overall record. The only loss came back in 1998, and the two sides tied in 2003 when Gary Player and Jack Nicklaus served as the team captains.

NBC and the Golf Channel hold the broadcast rights for the Presidents Cup.

Thursday, Sept. 24 Golf Channel | 12:30 - 7 p.m. ET

Friday, Sept. 25 Golf Channel | 2 - 7 p.m. ET

Saturday, Sept. 26 Golf Channel | 8 - 9 a.m. ET NBC | 9 a.m. - 7 p.m. ET

The Ryder Cup will return next fall, when the Americans and Europeans square off at Adare Manor in Ireland. That tournament will start on Sept. 17, 2027.

articles.title: Forget Steph Curry, Warriors have six players who ‘know how to win’, says Gary Payton II
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors fell at the Play-In Tournament stage in 2026. But Gary Payton II believes they could win the NBA Championship in 2027.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors fell at the Play-In Tournament stage in 2026. But Gary Payton II believes they could win the NBA Championship in 2027.

The NBA Western Conference could be dominated by the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder again this year. Nobody is giving the Golden State Warriors a chance – except the players themselves.

The big problem with the Warriors is that Steph Curry and Draymond Green are 'too old' and have not been surrounded by enough top-tier young players.

More recently, the Warriors have been leaning into their weakness. 33 year-old Gary Payton II believes that adding more veterans around Curry has actually helped the team.

Speaking to the San Francisco Chronicle , he says that the core of six veteran players – not including himself – can help Steph Curry cause a major upset this season.

Payton II explained: "I know they wanted to build that veteran core to help those young guys carry over. with Al ( Horford ), KP."

"When we get Jimmy back, and Dray, and Melt (De'Anthony Melton). Georges ( Niang ) … just a bunch of guys that know what it takes to win. And it's kinda starting to feel like that 2022 year, when we didn't have any expectations, and everybody counted us out."

Jimmy Butler is not expected back from his torn ACL until January, and his return will give the team a vital mid-season boost at a critical time heading into the All-Star break. The Warriors just need to stay competitive until then.

Warriors have an exciting youth player too

The Warriors recent high draft picks failed to change their course, with James Wiseman and Jonathan Kuminga enduring different degrees of difficulty.

But there is fresh hope with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg , who was taken with the number 11th overall pick.

Lendeborg earned the Summer League MVP, and was recently praised by new associate coach Frank Vogel.

But there will be no pressure on him. Instead it will all be on the veterans.

Steph Curry will lead the team again. He still averaged 26.6 points per game last season. But he does need a healthy Jimmy Butler, and all of the other players mentioned by Gary Payton II too.

And even then, it probably won't be enough.

articles.title: Presidents Cup Gives Medinah ‘Mount Rushmore’ of Major Golf Events
articles.summary: The Presidents Cup begins Thursday just outside Chicago.
articles.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — When the Presidents Cup tees off this Thursday, Medinah Country Club's famous Course No. 3 will become the first golf venue to host at least one edition of the Presidents Cup, Ryder Cup, PGA Championship, and U.S. Open.

"There's a tremendous amount of pride to have that Mount Rushmore of events on our shelves," Medinah host committee chairman Mike Scimo tells Front Office Sports .

Seven other courses have hosted at least one edition of the Ryder Cup, PGA Championship, and U.S. Open. But Medinah No. 3's portfolio is more diverse than any other, as the suburban Chicago course has welcomed several other notable golf events in its history:

Former Western Open: 1939, 1962, and 1966

Medinah's 1,100-plus-person membership funded a $23 million renovation of its championship course that was completed in 2024 and led by OCM Golf, a design firm co-owned by President Cup International team captain Geoff Ogilvy. Overall, membership has invested "well north" of $100 million into transforming the club since the 2012 Ryder Cup, Scimo says.

Medinah president David Latham tells FOS the club has tried to "reimagine" what types of golf events it can host in the future. "Getting tournaments is a hard business," Latham says.

U.S. Open venues are mostly set through 2050, and the PGA Championship's move from August to May in 2019 makes another edition at Medinah unlikely due to the risk of unfriendly springtime weather in the Chicago area. The Ryder Cup's next open U.S. date is 2041.

Latham says Medinah is in talks to host another tournament that has yet to be announced, but he pointed to major women's, collegiate, and amateur events as future targets for the club.

The PGA Tour operates the Presidents Cup , and the tour's shift to a new two-track model with a top-tier Championship Series and revamped Tour Championship is attractive to Medinah's long-term hosting goals, although Scimo says it's too early to tell what that could result in.

"We want the tournaments to be elevated in stature," Scimo says. "It will never be a tour stop—never. But if it's in that same once- or twice-a-decade timespan, and it's a special event—like a U.S. Amateur, like a Tour Championship, like a BMW Championship or an LPGA major—those are the type of marquee events that I think the members would rally around to continue to add to our legacy."

articles.title: J.J. Spaun, the 'odd man out,' was confused and frustrated after Presidents Cup snub
articles.summary: J.J. Spaun won the BMW PGA Championship on Sunday on the DP World Tour, and was the highest-ranked American left off the U.S. Team this week in Chicago.
articles.body:
J.J. Spaun was extremely confused, and a bit upset, after he didn't make the U.S. Presidents Cup team this fall.

That feeling didn't go away, especially after Spaun ran away with the BMW PGA Championship on the DP World Tour on Sunday. Spaun made four birdies in his last five holes to claim a two-shot win at the Wentworth Club.

"I played with a huge chip on my shoulder," Spaun said after the win. "I definitely had something to prove this week, but everything happens for a reason."

Spaun was the "odd man out" when Brandt Snedeker made his six captains picks to round out the U.S. team for this week's Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club in Chicago. Spaun was the highest-ranked player left off the team. Rookie Jackson Koivun made the squad, and Jacob Bridgeman — fresh off his win at the Biltmore Championship on Sunday — also made it in.

To Snedeker's credit, Spaun withdrew from last month's Tour Championship with a shoulder injury just days before he had to make the picks. But Spaun wasn't given a reason for being left off. He also said he was led to believe he'd be on the team based on good conversations he'd had with Snedeker throughout the year.

"It was like a 45-second phone call," Spaun said. "Just said I wasn't on the team, and said I was the odd man out and I wished him luck, and that was it."

Snedeker was asked about Spaun at Medinah on Tuesday. He quickly credited Spaun for his win, and said he's a "huge J.J. Spaun fan."

"The best advice I got from all the captains I talked to and even coaches, you've got to trust your gut. My gut was telling me one thing," Snedeker said. "You've got to make those decisions. It's tough. I feel awful for J.J., and I always will, because he's a great dude and I love the guy to death. "That being said, he's a competitor. Like I knew this was going to happen. I told all the guys that didn't make the team, like, 'Your job is to go make me look like an idiot as quick as possible.'"

"The best advice I got from all the captains I talked to and even coaches, you've got to trust your gut. My gut was telling me one thing," Snedeker said. "You've got to make those decisions. It's tough. I feel awful for J.J., and I always will, because he's a great dude and I love the guy to death.

"That being said, he's a competitor. Like I knew this was going to happen. I told all the guys that didn't make the team, like, 'Your job is to go make me look like an idiot as quick as possible.'"

Spaun has won three times on Tour in his career, most recently at the Valero Texas Open last season. He won the U.S. Open in 2025, too, and jumped to No. 12 in the Official World Golf Rankings after his DP World Tour win on Sunday.

The Americans will open the Presidents Cup on Thursday in Chicago with a series of four-ball matches. They've won the last 10 Presidents Cups, and have only actually lost to the International Team once in the event's history.

Spaun, though, will have to watch from home. His next shot at representing the United States will have to wait a year.

"I can't wait to see J.J. get off to a great start next year, and I would be shocked if he's not on the [Ryder Cup] team in Ireland," Snedeker said.

While it's far from the same thing, the win on Sunday certainly helped Spaun's mood.

"You know, being left off was obviously for a reason. I don't know what that reason was, but I'm here now and there was a reason why we're here," he said. "My caddie kept telling me that, and it's crazy how this has happened. You know, everything does happen for a reason. I'm just super happy."

articles.title: Presidents Cup: US team captain Brandt Snedeker wants JJ Spaun to 'make me look like an idiot' after snub
articles.summary: US team captain Brandt Snedeker responds to JJ Spaun’s comments after the former US Open champion was left out of the Presidents Cup team; watch the tournament live this week on Sky Sports Golf from Medinah Country Club
articles.body:
Spaun became just the third American to win the BMW PGA Championship , joining Arnold Palmer and Billy Horschel, and the first player to claim the title on their debut since Byeong-hun An in 2015.

The 36-year-old was controversially overlooked by Snedeker for a place in his side to face the International Team in the biennial match-play event, which pits the best golfers from the United States against the top international players at Medinah Country Club and is live from Thursday on Sky Sports .

Spaun admitted he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" at Wentworth, saying he had a point to prove and that missing out on the Presidents Cup had added fuel to his fire.

"Being a captain, you have to make tough decisions, unfortunately, and we had 15 or 16 guys that we were really looking at," said Snedeker, who also named Ryan Gerard, Akshay Bhatia and Gary Woodland - a US team vice-captain at this year's Presidents Cup - as close calls during his deliberations over the captain's picks.

"You're going to have to make these tough decisions and the best advice I got from all the guys I talked to, even coaches, is you got to trust your gut," Snedeker added. "My gut was telling me one thing."

The 12-man US team includes 21-year-old PGA Tour rookie Jackson Koivun and Ryder Cup veteran Patrick Cantlay, despite both finishing outside the top 12 in the Presidents Cup points standings. Last year's US Open champion Spaun, 36, was overlooked despite finishing 10th.

The American also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open, having made his Team USA debut at last September's Ryder Cup.

Spaun said he had good conversations with Snedeker during the qualification campaign and believed he would feature at Medinah, but was handed the unwanted news in a brief phone call after the season-ending Tour Championship.

"It was like a 45-second phone call," Spaun revealed in his press conference. "Just said I wasn't on the team and said I was the odd man out. I wished him luck and that was it.

"It [past conversations] led me to believe that I would make the team."

Spaun added: "I was pretty determined this week to kind of prove something. My whole career, I've kind of had to do that. I wasn't given scholarships. I had to earn my PGA Tour card the hard way. I was never given sponsor invite opportunities - I just had to do everything the hard way.

"Being left off was obviously for a reason. I don't know what that reason was, but I'm here now and there was a reason why we're here. My caddie kept telling me that and it's crazy how this has happened."

articles.title: Packers’ Jordan Love Faces Alarming NFL-Worst Problem After OT Escape
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers escaped New Jersey with a win.Their offensive line didn’t escape the scrutiny that followed.Two numbers released Monday painted a grim...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers escaped New Jersey with a win.

Their offensive line didn't escape the scrutiny that followed.

Two numbers released Monday painted a grim picture of the protection in front of Jordan Love . Analytics guru Ryan Paganetti ranked Green Bay last in the NFL with an 18% pass block win rate through Week 2.

RotoWire's Ian Hartitz then noted that the Packers' average time to pressure allowed was 2.36 seconds, also 32nd in the league.

The 18% mark leaves the Packers four percentage points behind the 31st-ranked Arizona Cardinals and 17 points behind the Baltimore Ravens in 30th. It's rare to see such separation after only two games, regardless of opponent or sample size.

The two figures reinforce each other. ESPN defines pass block win rate as the percentage of blocks sustained for at least 2.5 seconds. Green Bay's average pressure is coming before that threshold.

It's a dangerous world to live in for a team whose hopes are tethered to Love.

The Packers rallied from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the New York Jets 20-17 in overtime Sunday, but Love finished with 145 passing yards. Green Bay managed 199 total yards and converted one of nine third downs.

Packers' Protection Problem Goes Past Sack Total

Love's ability to avoid sacks can soften the appearance of a breakdown. Pressure still influences his feet, timing and options, even when he gets rid of the football.

That distinction became obvious during Green Bay's 39-22 season-opening loss to the Minnesota Vikings . Love was officially hit 15 times and sacked four times. Offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich counted 18 hits, while Matt LaFleur called some of the protection failures "busts that absolutely should not and cannot happen."

Green Bay adjusted against New York, leaning on quicker throws and moving pockets. Love absorbed one sack, although the offense scrambled to stay on schedule. He needed a late defensive stand, a 63-yard punt return and three double-digit gains in overtime to pull out the victory.

The time-to-pressure trend makes the opening fortnight harder to dismiss as one bad afternoon against an hostile Vikings defense. Green Bay ranked fifth in that category in 2023 at 2.64 seconds and fifth again in 2024 at 2.63. The Packers slipped to 21st at 2.55 seconds last season before falling to 2.36 through two games in 2026.

Injuries Give Packers a Short Time to Find Answers

The situation grew more complicated during the Jets game.

Starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele injured his knee on Green Bay's opening series. LaFleur said afterward that the injury didn't look good and Bako-Bewele "could be out for a long time."

Starting left guard Aaron Banks later exited with a toe injury. His replacement, Donovan Jennings , then hurt his hand, forcing rookie Jager Burton into the lineup. Rookie Anthony Belton replaced Bako-Bewele.

Losing Bako-Bewele would remove the group's steadiest piece. He started 51 games over his first four seasons and helped Green Bay rank second in sacks allowed and third in sack percentage from 2023 through 2025, per his Packers biography .

The Packers listed Bako-Bewele, Banks and Jennings as estimated nonparticipants on Monday's injury report .

With no full practice and a Thursday night home opener against the Atlanta Falcons looming, the coaching staff has not much of a shot to create cohesion.

Love has shown he can rescue an bumpy afternoon.

But Green Bay can't make survival his weekly assignment.

articles.title: Is Micah Parsons Practicing Yet? Packers Make Call Before Falcons
articles.summary: A new NFL rule made Micah Parsons eligible to return to practice after Week 2. Green Bay has decided not to make that move yet. The post Is Micah Parsons Pra...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers technically had the option to take a significant step toward getting Micah Parsons back this week.

Parsons remains on the physically unable to perform list as Green Bay prepares to host the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night. More importantly, he was not added to the Packers' Week 3 injury report, an indication that the team has yet to open his return-to-practice window.

The same is true for tight end Luke Musgrave and defensive lineman Jordon Riley , Green Bay's other two players on the PUP list.

"Worth noting – none of the 3 players on PUP have been added to the injury report, which means they have not opened their 'return to practice' windows. Micah Parsons was the most-talked about of the group as potentially returning after week 2, but so far it's a no-go," Packers cap analyst Ken Ingalls wrote Tuesday.

There is an important distinction between Parsons returning to practice and returning to a game.

What Micah Parsons' Absence From Injury Report Means

The NFL changed its PUP rules for 2026, allowing players on reserve/PUP to begin a 21-day practice window after their team's second regular-season game.

That means Parsons became eligible to practice after Sunday's 20-17 overtime win over the New York Jets .

Players placed on reserve/PUP must miss at least the first four games of the season, meaning Parsons was already ruled out for both Thursday's matchup with Atlanta and Green Bay's Week 4 game regardless of whether he practiced this week.

Once the Packers designate Parsons to return, however, a 21-day clock begins. Green Bay would then have that period to activate him to the 53-man roster.

The Packers apparently aren't ready to start it.

Head coach Matt LaFleur hinted at that possibility last week when asked when Parsons could return to practice.

"I haven't even asked about that," LaFleur said, per The Leap's Jason B. Hirschhorn. "Probably a couple weeks."

That timeline also fits what Parsons has said about his recovery.

Parsons tore his ACL in December and later revealed he also underwent a meniscus procedure. The Packers have been following a nine-month recovery guideline because of the additional damage to his knee.

"We have a pretty strong nine-month rule," Parsons said earlier this month.

Packers' Short Week Could Explain Parsons Decision

Green Bay's schedule makes waiting another few days even more understandable.

The Packers played an overtime game against the Jets on Sunday and host Atlanta only four days later. They didn't hold a full practice Monday, with their first injury report based on estimated participation.

That leaves very little meaningful practice time for Parsons before Thursday.

Opening his 21-day window now would start the clock during a week in which he would get limited full-speed work and still wouldn't be eligible to play against Atlanta.

The Packers will have considerably more time after Thursday night's game before returning to action.

That could give Green Bay a better opportunity to open Parsons' window and begin a legitimate ramp-up instead of using several days of it during a shortened practice week.

The Packers have not publicly said the short week is the reason for waiting, so that remains a logical explanation rather than a confirmed one.

What is clear is that Parsons isn't coming back against Atlanta.

He was never eligible to play Thursday under the PUP rules.

The more meaningful development is that Green Bay could have started getting him back onto the practice field this week and, at least so far, has chosen not to.

articles.body:
A scary injury to wide receiver Jayden Reed dampened the Green Bay Packers ' 20-17 win over the New York Jets on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford.

The former Michigan State Spartans wideout was carted off the field in the first half of the game after absorbing a hit to the head and neck area. He was stretchered off the field and was ruled out for the rest of the contest. However, he showed movement in his extremities, which was a great sign, relatively speaking.

It remains to be seen when Reed can return to action . Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday, "It's way too early for that right now," with regard to the wide receiver's timeline (h/t Rob Demovsky of ESPN).

"He's got a lot going on," added LaFleur, who at least noted that Reed did indeed suffer a neck injury.

Reed, who signed a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension with the Packers in April, only had four receiving yards on a catch and a target before leaving the meeting with the Jets. Through two games in 2026, he has 24 receiving yards on four receptions and eight targets.

The 26-year-old Reed is unfortunately dealing with an unwanted scenario reminiscent of what he went through in 2025. Last season, he suffered an injury in a Week 2 game against the Washington Commanders and missed several games, but he returned in Week 13 and finished the campaign.

For now, Reed can be expected to miss Green Bay's Week 3 showdown against the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field, with the game scheduled for Thursday.

articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — The New York Mets placed starter Christian Scott on the 15-day injured list Tuesday, ending the right-hander's season because of left knee inflammation.

Devin Williams was activated from the IL after not pitching since Aug. 7 because of a right shoulder strain.

Andy Green, after being named the Mets full-time manager , said Scott had a slight dip in velocity during his last start against Philadelphia after slipping on the mound while warming up Saturday.

"Didn't tell anybody and knee swelled up on him, and it's not right to push through anything at this stage of the season," Green said. "Don't think there's anything long-term here, but it is enough that it doesn't make sense for him to make his next start."

After missing all of 2025 recovering from Tommy John surgery, Scott went 4-5 with a 3.85 ERA in 23 starts this season. He had 134 strikeouts in 111 innings.

Williams is 3-2 with a 4.66 ERA and 16 saves in 42 appearances during his first season with the Mets. A two-time All-Star closer, the right-hander signed a $51 million, three-year deal in December shortly before incumbent closer Edwin Díaz left New York for the Los Angeles Dodgers as a free agent.

Green said the last-place Mets hope to get Williams in a couple of games before the seasons ends Sunday. Kodai Senga has been closing games in his absence.

"I think long term we know what role he will slide back into, but for these outings I don't think we're overly concerned about that," Green said. "We just want to get him back on the mound pitching again and he's done a lot of work to get to that point."
